subject: Feature basket recomposition & stepdown guardrails
messages:
From: Claire Raymond <claire@clearmind.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearmind.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Replatforming: Simplifying plans and avoiding stepdown surprises

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for last week's demo. We like Redwood's performance, but our procurement team pushed back on the number of SKUs and the risk when downgrading tiers.

Can you share a proposal that simplifies the 'feature basket' for our two primary use cases (Core Inference + Audit logs) and spell out what happens if we stepdown later (feature removal, data retention, SLA changes)? Procurement will need clear guardrails to approve the purchase.

I've attached our current SOW for reference (clearmind-sow.pdf).

Primary priorities:
- Keep latency SLAs for customer-facing inference
- Preserve audit/history for at least 90 days in any downgrade path
- Clear list of 'must-have' vs 'nice-to-have' features

Appreciate a strawman we can share with legal/procurement by next week.

Best,

Claire Raymond
Director of AI Product, ClearMind Health
claire@clearmind.ai
(415) 555-0198

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Claire Raymond <claire@clearmind.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Replatforming: Simplifying plans and avoiding stepdown surprises

Hi Claire — thanks for the SOW and context.

I've put together an initial 'feature-basket' recomposition and two stepdown guardrail options attached (feature-basket-proposal-v2.pdf). High level:
- Offer A: Consolidated Core tier (Inference + 90d audit) + opt-in addons (Dedicated KV cache, Extended retention)
- Offer B: Usage-first plan (metered tokens) with retention as an addon — less predictable unit economics but lower up-front cost

We'll call out which features are non-negotiable for latency/SLA and which can be gated behind addons. Ben has drafted the pricing scenarios; Ben — can you confirm the stepdown credit logic (monthly proration + feature credit) in the attached spreadsheet?

Next steps:
1) We'll align on which features are 'must' for your production apps
2) We propose a canary downgrade policy (30-day canary + auto-fallback to last known good model if performance regresses)
3) We will produce a short one-pager you can circulate to procurement/legal

Can we target a review call Monday 11/1 10am PT?

Cheers,

Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com
Schedule: https://redwood.com/hannah/schedule

Attachment: feature-basket-proposal-v2.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Replatforming: Simplifying plans and avoiding stepdown surprises

Hannah / team — attached is a pricing grid with three modeled scenarios: Consolidated Core, Usage-first, and Hybrid (base + burst credits). Key notes:
- Stepdown credits: we propose feature credits that are applied to remaining term (not cash refunds) — standard approach for modular features
- SLA delta: downgrades that remove Dedicated KV cache will carry a documented SLA uplift risk; we quantify expected p95 increase per workload bucket (see sheet 'latency-impact')
- Retention addon: 90d retention included in Core; 365d as paid addon with KMS support

Questions for ClearMind:
- Which workload bucket is primary (low-latency interactive vs batch)? That will change cost favorability
- Any procurement constraints around non-monetary credits vs cash refunds?

Attachment: pricing-grid-clearmind.xlsx

Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
Phone: (650) 555-0112

From: Claire Raymond <claire@clearmind.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearmind.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Replatforming: Simplifying plans and avoiding stepdown surprises

Thanks — attaching internal priorities (clearmind-priorities.docx). Quick answers:
- Primary workload is interactive inference (low-latency, ~60k qps monthly peak)
- Procurement prefers cash refunds where material, but will accept feature credits for up to 25% of committed value in year 1
- Audit/data retention must be preserved for 90 days; permanent deletion is only permitted after a documented data-retention policy

Two asks before review call:
1) Can Redwood commit to a written downgrade runbook that lists exactly which features/entitlements change and how to restore them?
2) If a downgrade causes SLA regressions, what remediation credits are available (service credits + engineering support hours)?

On the call Monday we'll invite our Head of Procurement and Director of Security.

Best,

Claire

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Claire Raymond <claire@clearmind.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Replatforming: Simplifying plans and avoiding stepdown surprises

Claire — thanks for the clarity. Short answers and proposed guardrails below; we'll walk through on the 11/1 10am PT call.

1) Downgrade runbook (we will deliver a doc pre-call):
- Exact feature map per SKU (what toggles off/on)
- Data retention & export steps (90d snapshot, retention extension addon)
- Automated fallback: if p95 latency increases >20% during a stepdown, traffic will automatically route to the previously pinned model for up to 72 hours while we remediate

2) Remediation credits:
- SLA regression caused solely by downgrade: 10% service credit of monthly fee for the impacted month + 8 engineering hours of priority support
- SLA regression due to incompatibility at deployment: we will provide root-cause report and case-by-case support credits
- Procurement note: feature credits available up to 25% of committed value in year 1 (Ben's spreadsheet models this)

Proposed agenda for the call (30 min):
- 10:00-10:05 — Introductions
- 10:05-10:10 — ClearMind priorities (Claire)
- 10:10-10:20 — Redwood proposal (Hannah + Ben) — feature basket + pricing scenarios
- 10:20-10:28 — Downgrade runbook & SLA credit mechanics (Jonas)
- 10:28-10:30 — Next steps and procurement action items (Lauren)

Attachments we will circulate after the call: final one-pager for procurement, runbook draft, pricing grid exported to PDF.

See you Monday — invite accepted.

Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.com
Attachment: feature-basket-proposal-v2.pdf

--
